akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرْضَعَتْ﴾: that is because He meant — and Allah knows best — the act; had He meant the attribute, as we see it, He would have said "مُرْضِع" (a nursing woman). Likewise every "مُفْعِل" and "فَاعِل" that applies to the female and not to the male is without hāʾ, such as "مُقْرِب" (near to giving birth) and "مُوقِر": (as in) نَخْلَةٌ مُوقِرٌ (a heavily laden palm), "مُشْدِن" (a doe that has a fawn with her), "حامِل" (pregnant), "حائِض" (menstruating), "فادك", "طامِث" (menstruating) and "طالِق" (divorced).

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِ﴾: ﴿يَدْعُو﴾ is equivalent to "يَقُول" (he says), and ﴿مَنْ﴾ is nominative, with the khabar (predicate) implied, as though: "he says: he whose harm is nearer than his benefit is his god". He means: "he whose harm is nearer than his benefit — his god".

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ مَا يَغِيظُ﴾: He omitted the hāʾ (the object pronoun) from ﴿يَغِيظُ﴾ because it is in the ṣila (relative clause) of "الذي" (which); since the whole has become a single noun, omission is lighter.

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿هَـٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُواْ﴾ because they were two parties. "الخَصْمُ" (adversary) can be singular and plural.

akhfash:25-25.t:
And He said ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ﴾: its meaning is "whoever intends deviation". He added the bāʾ as it is added in His word ﴿تَنبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ﴾. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 252]:
ألَيْسَ أَمِيرِي في الأُمورِ بأَنْتُمَا * بِمَالَسْتُما أَهْلَ الخِيانَةِ والغَدْرِ
(Are you two not my commander in affairs, with what you (are), not being people of betrayal and treachery?)

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿فَٱجْتَنِبُواْ ٱلرِّجْسَ مِنَ ٱلأَوْثَانِ﴾, and all of them are filth; the meaning is: "so avoid the filth that comes from them", i.e. worshipping them.

akhfash:36-36.t: And He said ﴿صَوَآفَّ﴾: its singular is "الصافَّة" (standing in a row).

akhfash:40-40.t:
And He said ﴿لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَاتٌ وَمَسَاجِدُ﴾: prayers are not demolished, but He construed it on another verb, as though He said "and prayers would have been abandoned". Some said: "He means only the places of prayer". A man among the transmitters from al-Ḥasan read ﴿صُلُوتٌ﴾ and said: "They are the synagogues of the Jews, called in Hebrew 'ṣulūthā'; this is the meaning of 'al-ṣalawāt' as they explained it."
And He said ﴿وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾, because ﴿بَعْضَهُم﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ﴿الناس﴾.

akhfash:45-45.t: And He said ﴿وَبِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَّشِيدٍ﴾: He construed it on ﴿كَأَيِّنْ﴾ (how many). "المَشِيد" is the passive participle of "شِدتُه" (I built it high), "أَنَا أشِيدُهُ" (I build it high), like "عِنْتُه" (I struck him with the evil eye), "أَنَا أَعِينُه", so "هو مَعِين".

akhfash:47-47.t: And He said ﴿وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ﴾: He means "in heaviness and in what is feared of it, it is like a thousand years".

akhfash:72-72.t: And He said ﴿بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ﴾: nominative as an explanation, i.e. "it is the Fire". Had it been genitive as a badal (substitute), it would have been good.

akhfash:73-73.t: And He said ﴿ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فَٱسْتَمِعُواْ لَهُ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَن يَخْلُقُواْ ذُبَاباً وَلَوِ ٱجْتَمَعُواْ لَهُ﴾. If it is asked: "Where then is the likeness?", I say: there is no likeness here, because He, Blessed and Exalted, said (in effect): "A likeness was struck for Me, and it was made a likeness to Me in their view; so listen to this likeness that they made a likeness of Me in their saying and in their taking of gods, and (know) that they will never be able to create a fly even if they gathered together for it; and they are so weak that if the fly snatched something from them and they all gathered to rescue it from it, they would not be able to do that. So how can these gods be struck as a likeness for their Lord, while He is the Lord of everything, the One, like unto whom there is nothing, who is with everything and nearer than everything, who has no resemblance, no likeness and no equal, and He is the Most High, the Most Great, the One, the Lord who has ever been and ever will be."

akhfash:78-78.t: And He said ﴿مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾: accusative as a command (i.e. "follow").
